decisions.reason: SOL combines the horn’s arrival and the recognition naturally without losing the thought.
SOL already incorporates the deleted sentence’s recognition into H001.
SOL adds “of the world,” which the source does not specify.
The subject is clear from context; omitting the repeated name preserves the source’s meaning.
The charging elephants and unmistakable swinging trunks preserve the image.
The terse identification preserves the reveal.
SOL preserves the creatures’ size and strength and the land-and-river comparison.
The source says people regarded elephants as mysterious; “with wonder” changes that attitude.
SOL preserves the shared life with animals, their training, and the tusks carved into horns.
“In triumph” changes the source’s excited, uplifted reaction into victory.
The shorter shout keeps the same taunt and voice.
The subject remains clear, and SOL retains the nervous watching and fifteen-minute timing.
“Let’s have a proper fight” naturally conveys the challenge and the improved numbers.
“Confident” preserves the source’s assurance.
The reordered sentence preserves the timing and cause.
“A migration on a staggering scale” preserves the mass movement and its magnitude.
The sequence and abandonment of the ancestral homeland remain intact.
SOL retains Yayul Cheok’s anger, grief, and gratitude without changing their substance.
“United at last” preserves the unification, oath, and departure.
“Many” weakens the source’s emphatic abundance of ferocious beasts.
The source states that their appearance means something; SOL makes it conditional.
The groups coming together and the threat retain the source’s meaning.
SOL preserves the clenched fist and the allies’ change from fear to hope.
“Have a proper fight” keeps the spoken challenge intact.
The source describes the Palace’s forces as a small kingdom, not the Palace itself.
SOL preserves both groups’ prior despair or hope and their sudden cheering.
The darker gaze amid the joy preserves Namho’s contrasting reaction.
The thought retains the concern that Sichuan’s factions could not have left it undefended.
SOL drops Namho’s seasoned gaze, a characterization detail in the source.
The reordered noun phrase preserves the Palace’s strength and Sichuan’s damaged state.
The reason he thought they could not come remains clear.
“Front lines that extensive” preserves the source’s broad-front concern.
SOL introduces a snow-covered mountainside before the source’s later snow imagery.
“By now” preserves the enemy’s transformation and the boulder’s imminent threat.
“Couldn’t have found a way” preserves the Alliance’s lack of a rescue solution.
The awl image and the danger of even a slight gap remain.
SOL preserves the deep penetration and the Moving Formation mechanism.
The comparison to every other Central Plains region is intact.
“Could hardly have been more dire” preserves the source’s emphatic severity.
SOL retains that ghostlike enemies are not the only threat Sichuan faces.
“Base” conveys the abandoned stronghold, and the route through Sichuan remains clear.
SOL carries the moment cue into H043, avoiding a redundant standalone transition.
SOL drops the repeated, tangled motion of Namho’s thoughts before they vanish.
The casual exclamation preserves his admiration and relief at having stayed.
Deleting “It was him” loses the source’s emphatic recognition beat after “Great Sir.”
“Stubbornly held his position” preserves the source’s deliberate steadfastness; “remained” weakens it.
The casual question preserves both the breathless-place remark and the head-shaving observation.
The referent is clear from the immediately preceding identification as Great Sir.
SOL omits the source’s detail that the distant cloud was slowly drawing nearer.
SOL preserves that only his Supreme Peak eyesight could pick out the scene.
The source’s standalone “No” supplies a deliberate correction beat before the more precise view.
The people advancing behind the elephants preserves the source’s elephants-leading-the-way arrangement.
SOL omits that he added this observation after staring at them.
“A bit like monks” preserves the tentative comparison.
The source’s moment cue sets the timing of the shout and is not repeated in SOL.
SOL keeps the agent’s age and the surprising volume of his shout.
“Goddamn bastard” preserves the source’s forceful profanity.
“At the same moment” preserves the simultaneous action.
The elephants leading the charge preserves the source’s formation.
“Tens of thousands of li” accurately preserves the source’s distance; BASE substitutes miles.
The grammatical recast preserves the Potala Palace as a religious group living in its own world.
SOL says the Palace appeared inside the cloud; the source identifies it as the cloud’s identity.
The simultaneous trumpeting and mad charge remain intact.
The blackened tusks and uncontrolled eyes preserve the grotesque appearance.
“Felt it again” preserves the narrator’s renewed realization.
The zoo memory still places him as a child with his mother.
“All of it” preserves the emphatic summary.
The comma simply clarifies the reference to Dumbo without changing the joke.
The stronger phrasing matches the source’s blunt profanity rather than softening it.
The title retains the joke that the baby elephant is outrageously strong.
The ground splitting open preserves the escalation from shaking to cracking.
SOL integrates Cheongpung’s spoken reaction without losing his dazed assessment.
The dialogue is retained in H072, so deleting its duplicate is faithful.
Italicizing the narrator’s internal reaction follows the project’s thought convention.
“Nearly escaped” preserves the almost-spoken reaction without changing its force.
The source says the encirclement holds regardless of the Potala Palace’s approach; SOL changes this concession into a contrast.
SOL adds “now,” which the source does not specify.
SOL invents “For me,” reversing the source’s direct statement that the arrival is terrible luck for them.
The source’s “too” explicitly marks the Potala Palace as an additional force joining Dark Heaven.
SOL combines the considered possibility and the low odds without changing the meaning.
SOL already includes the low-odds thought in H080.
“So had most people” clearly refers to the belief that the possibility was unlikely.
“Drawn out of Tibet” changes the source’s emphasis on recruiting a group that had been staying there.
The concise transition preserves the reversal.
The source says the Lord’s objective was pursued through the events in Qinghai; SOL recasts it as something wanted from Qinghai.
The clipped repetition preserves the narrator’s realization that he was the target.
The realization and the weight pressing on his chest remain intact.
“It ache” gives the ache an unclear referent; the source says the weight makes the narrator ache.
The spontaneous question remains, with the natural implication that it slipped from his lips.
The Blood Lord’s understanding and ready answer are preserved; the contrast marker is not needed.
SOL replaces the named Lord of Heaven with “he,” losing the explicit title in the source.
The exclamation mark preserves the source’s startled reaction.
The sequence is retained by “Then” in H094, making the standalone transition redundant.
“Then” preserves the transition into the Blood Lord’s Sound Transmission.
“One day from now” can mean a future point in time; the source promises a day’s time starting now.
The Blood Lord is the clear subject from the previous sentence, and the gesture and smile remain.
SOL drops the source’s explicit “that person” reference and recasts the protected wording.
“That was the end of it” preserves the source’s finality more precisely than “That was all.”
The source’s stabbing image in the narrator’s chest is more specific than SOL’s “cut deep.”
